summary_of_pdf: The document is a formal administrative claim under DFARS 227.7004 submitted by a pro se inventor, Reinaldo Aguiar Marcano, alleging that Lockheed Martin Corporation is infringing upon his pending patent applications in the development of the F-35 Technology Refresh 3 (TR-3) and various quantum computing initiatives. The claimant asserts he has granted a perpetual, no-fee license to the U.S. Department of Defense for these technologies, and therefore alleges that Lockheed Martin is committing procurement fraud by charging the government for intellectual property the government already possesses the right to use. The document demands an immediate halt to procurement payments and threatens contracting officers and corporate counsel with criminal liability and ethical sanctions.
attorneys_comments: Upon careful review, this administrative claim exhibits the hallmarks of a legally deficient, pro se demand. The claimant relies entirely on pending, unissued patent applications (the 19/ series) to assert infringement and demand compensation. Under 35 U.S.C. § 154(d), provisional rights require actual issuance of a patent and actual notice of the published claims, making this demand highly premature and legally unenforceable at this juncture. Furthermore, the claimant fundamentally misconstrues 28 U.S.C. § 1498, which waives sovereign immunity for the government's use of issued patents, not pending applications. The allegations of procurement fraud are predicated on a unilateral, unsolicited 'license grant' of unissued rights, which does not legally encumber Lockheed Martin's contractual billing. The threats directed at Procuring Contracting Officers (PCOs) regarding criminal liability, as well as the invocation of SEC disclosure requirements and ABA Model Rule 8.3 against corporate counsel, are frivolous intimidation tactics lacking evidentiary or statutory merit. The evidentiary strength of the claim is negligible pending actual patent issuance and a rigorous Markman construction of any allowed claims.
recommended_next_steps: Counsel for Lockheed Martin and the relevant DoD agencies should formally acknowledge receipt of the communication to preclude any default administrative escalation under DFARS 227.7004, while unequivocally denying the claims on the basis that no patents have issued. Do not engage in substantive technical discussions or element-by-element rebuttals, as doing so may inadvertently create an evidentiary record for future litigation. Docket the cited USPTO application serial numbers (19/639,219; 19/560,038; 19/562,838; 19/562,845) for routine monitoring to track potential issuance. File this communication within the respective procurement files to document the baseless nature of the fraud allegations.
